body:
**Starts** once #53 is merged.

## Why

A stop that runs on a timetable, such as a boat or a tour, is fixed at a time even before its timetable is published. The coordinator's instructions don't say so. They say: "Give a stop a set time only when it's fixed at that time, such as a dinner reservation or a sunrise hike. Most stops have none." So when the departure time isn't known, the coordinator leaves the stop with no set time. The schedule then puts it wherever the day has room, as with any stop that follows the one before it. The result looks like a plan but protects nothing: other stops can push the boat around, and workers read its made-up time as real.

The fix is small and clear: have the coordinator propose a likely time and length for a timetable stop, ask the user, give the stop that set time, and say it's a placeholder to check once the timetable is out. This issue checks that the fix works, with an evaluation before and after it. Joe picked it as an easy case to learn evaluations on.

## What happened

Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30, agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`, in the `road-trip-agent` project in Phoenix. The trip is a 4-day loop from Natick, MA, with two nights in Bar Harbor. A whale watch on Friday, Day 2, was one of the things the user wanted most.

1. **Turn 4** (turn span `d166ae54f4b36d18`). The coordinator added a "whale watching cruise" stop, and selected Bar Harbor Whale Watch Co with `select_user_place`, a 4-hour visit time, and no set time. Google had no hours for it. Day 2 starts at 7:00 a.m., so the schedule put the boat at 7:03 a.m. The reply said: "I don't know the 2027 departure times yet, so the schedule has the boat leaving right after breakfast. Once the company posts its spring schedule, we can set the real time."
2. **Turn 5.** A stay researcher filling Friday's breakfast read the 7:03 time as real. It ruled out one café as "impractical before a 7:03 whale watch", and noted another's "sit-down service may be slow before a 7:03 tour."
3. **Turn 14.** After breakfast was picked, the boat moved to 8:05. The user asked: "When would the whale tour be on Friday, it says 7:05? [...] wouldn't it be at 7am or not 7:05?"
4. **Turn 15** (turn span `82d5c767c99ad6c5`). The user asked: "Can't we base the whale watching on this year's departure time/schedule? [...] For now it seems like we are just hoping it works out based on what time we end up having free." The coordinator sent a stay researcher to look for past schedules. It found none, but found the season start, trip lengths of 3 to 5½ hours, and summer departures around 8 a.m., noon, and 4 p.m. Only then did the coordinator propose planning Friday around a set departure. In turn 16 the user chose the 8 a.m. boat, and the coordinator gave the stop a set time.

Joe's read: the whale watch was an undefined block with a label on it, not protected and not representing anything. The coordinator should have proposed a block in turn 4, such as "I can't find the departure times until they're posted. What if we block out 4 hours from 8:00 to 12:00, and adjust when the schedule is out?"

## The fix to test

Change the set time rule in the coordinator's instructions, in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and technical spec 5.2: a stop that runs on a timetable, such as a boat or a tour, gets a set time even when the timetable isn't out yet. Propose a likely time and length from what's typical, ask the user, set it once they agree, and say it's a placeholder to check later. Saving that it's a placeholder to trip memory may fit too. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), section 5.2 (laying out days: set times).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), a stop's `setTime`.
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- How is the situation set up? Proposal: start from a saved trip like this one after turn 3: the Bar Harbor stay, Day 2 staying put in Bar Harbor, and no whale watch stop yet. Send one message that asks for a whale watch with Bar Harbor Whale Watch Co on Friday, with no time given. The company's place has no hours on Google, as here.
- What counts as a pass? Proposal: a pass is the whale watch stop with a set time, or a reply that proposes a time and length and asks the user, without leaving the boat to follow the stop before it. A fail is a selected whale watch with no set time and no question about the time. Checked from what was saved, plus a judge model for the reply.
- How many runs before and after? Proposal: 10 each, as in #167.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, and run it on the current instructions for the baseline. Record the results in this issue.
- If the baseline passes almost every run, the change still goes in, since the gap in the instructions is clear. The evaluation then catches it if it comes back.
- Make the instruction change. Run `npm run agent-views`, and commit the coordinator's view file with it.
- Run the evaluation again, and record the results in the PR.

## Done when

- The baseline and the after results are both recorded, with how many runs passed in each.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat.
